prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” roofing company for everyone in Dallas — the right contractor depends on your priorities (budget, materials, warranty, speed, insurance-help, etc.). I can, however, help you find the best option for your situation by giving:

- A short checklist of what to require from any roofer
- How to verify legitimacy and quality
- Red flags to avoid
- Next steps (I can look up highly rated local contractors if you tell me your ZIP code)

Quick checklist for choosing a Dallas roof replacement contractor
1. Licensing & insurance
   - Ask for a current State of Texas contractor license (if applicable) and proof of general liability and workers’ comp insurance. Get a certificate of insurance and call the carrier to verify.
2. Manufacturer certifications
   - Prefer contractors certified by major shingle makers (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning). Certification means access to stronger warranties and approved installation methods.
3. Written estimate & contract
   - Get at least 3 detailed written estimates including scope (remove vs overlay), materials, warranty (material and workmanship), start/end dates, payment schedule, and permitting responsibilities.
4. References & reviews
   - Check recent online reviews (Google, Yelp), BBB rating, and ask for local references from similar jobs.
5. Permits & inspections
   - Contractor should obtain local permits and arrange required inspections. Confirm they will handle disposal of old shingles.
6. Warranty clarity
   - Distinguish manufacturer warranty (shingles) from workmanship warranty (contractor). Get warranties in writing.
7. Insurance claim experience (if storm damage)
   - If you’re filing a claim, ask whether the contractor will document damage and work directly with your insurer (but don’t let them pressure you to sign assignment-of-benefits without understanding it).

Red flags
- Extremely low bids compared to other quotes.
- Insistence on large cash-only upfront payment.
- No local address or no local references (storm-chasing crews sometimes move from storm to storm).
- No written contract or evasive answers about permits/warranties.
- High-pressure “sign today” sales tactics.

Where to verify reputation
- Google and Yelp reviews
- Better Business Bureau (BBB)
- Angi/HomeAdvisor
- Manufacturer locators (GAF, CertainTeed dealer locators)
- Texas Department of Licensing & Regulation (for trade-specific requirements) or city building permit records

If you want, I can:
- Pull up a short list of top-rated roofing contractors in your Dallas ZIP code (with links to reviews and certifications)
- Draft an email or phone script you can use when requesting estimates
- Provide a comparison checklist template for the bids you receive

Tell me your ZIP code and any priorities (budget, shingle brand, insurance claim, timeline) and I’ll find local options and tailor recommendations.
